title: SDK resilience presets, safe-idempotency patterns, and retry taxonomy with language examples
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines opinionated, cross-language defaults for client-side retry/backoff presets, a concise retryable-error taxonomy, and a safe idempotency contract for one-off and streaming operations across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. The goal is to provide predictable, production-safe defaults for most customers while offering knobs for advanced tuning (batching/latency trade-offs).

Goals:
- Ship three named retry profiles (conservative, balanced, aggressive) with numeric defaults and clear trade-offs documented.
- Standardize idempotency semantics: when SDK should auto-generate keys, when callers must provide them, and TTL/ledger semantics on server.
- Produce a clear retryable-error taxonomy (transient, rate-limited, capacity, client-fatal) with mappings to HTTP codes and SDK behavior.
- Define streaming ergonomics: resume tokens, when streaming is resumable vs non-idempotent, and recommended client patterns for reconnect.
- Provide concrete, minimal examples in Python/TS/Go and helper utilities that are ergonomic and auditable.

Design decisions / Proposal (high level):
1) Retry profiles (client presets):
   - conservative: max_retries=2, base_delay=200ms, max_delay=2s, jitter=full, total_retry_budget=5s. Use case: latency-sensitive user-facing requests where duplicate work is costly.
   - balanced: max_retries=4, base_delay=200ms, max_delay=5s, jitter=full, total_retry_budget=15s. Use case: standard inference calls for most customers.
   - aggressive: max_retries=8, base_delay=100ms, max_delay=10s, jitter=full, total_retry_budget=45s. Use case: background batches, bulk embeddings jobs that tolerate higher latency but reduce error rate.
   Rationale: Named presets make it easy to choose predictable defaults across SDKs and docs. Each preset includes both attempt limits and a wall-clock retry budget to bound tail latency.

2) Retryable error taxonomy (simplified):
   - transient_retriable: network timeouts, TCP resets, connection closed (map to client-level ECONN*/ETIMEDOUT), HTTP 502, 504. SDK: full retry according to profile.
   - rate_limited: HTTP 429 with Retry-After or 503 with rate hint. SDK: respect Retry-After if present, otherwise backoff per profile; consider early exit if Retry-After >> budget.
   - capacity_overload: explicit 503/capacity responses or server-provided throttle codes. SDK: treat like rate_limited but prefer exponential backoff with increased base_delay. Report metric tag 'capacity_rejection'.
   - optimistic_conflict: HTTP 409 for resource conflicts (idempotency mismatch). SDK: do not retry automatically; surface to caller with helper to reconcile.
   - client_error_nonretriable: 400, 401, 403, malformed request. SDK: fail fast; do not retry.
   - stream_resumeable_marker: streaming transport disconnects with server-sent resume token. SDK: attempt resume flow (see streaming section).

   Mapping is intentionally conservative: prefer not to perform silent retries on non-retriable client errors.

3) Idempotency: one-off (non-stream) calls
   - Contract: For operations that create or mutate server-side resources (e.g., fine-tune training job, long-running export), SDK will accept an Idempotency-Key header. If caller omits key, the SDK will auto-generate a v4 UUID for the lifetime of the request attempt and will reuse the same key across retries initiated by that single client call.
   - Auto-generation policy: SDK-generated keys are ephemeral (not persisted client-side) and only meant to dedupe server-side duplicate processing for retries of the same logical call. If caller needs cross-process dedupe, they must supply their own stable key.
   - Server TTL expectation: document that server will store idempotency result for at least 1 hour (recommendation), but server SLA is out-of-scope for SDK; SDK will expose idempotency metadata returned by server (idempotency_status, created_at) when available.
   - 409/IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH: if server returns a conflict because a key exists with differing payload, SDK surfaces a typed IdempotencyConflict error with the server response attached. This is non-retriable.

4) Idempotency and streaming semantics:
   - Streaming generation (token-by-token) is non-idempotent by default. Two main streaming models we support: resumable streams and pure live streams.
   - Resumable streams: Server emits a Resume-Token (string) and per-chunk sequence numbers. On transient disconnects, client can request resume by providing the Resume-Token and last sequence number received. SDK should expose a StreamResumeHelper that takes care of: local checkpointing, exponential reconnect, and replaying any final partial chunk. Resume attempts counted against the retry budget.
   - Non-resumable streams (typical websocket/long-poll): SDK must not auto-retry because duplicate tokens can produce diverging completions. Instead, SDK will surface a StreamDisconnected error and provide a small helper that callers can opt into to request a fresh generation (with new idempotency key) or to switch to polling.
   - Recommendation: For client libraries, expose two high-level APIs: generate_stream (best-effort non-resumable ergonomic streaming) and generate_resumable_stream (explicit resume contract with tokens).

5) Language ergonomics & examples (summary):
   - Python: provide a RetryProfile dataclass, a convenience decorator @redwood.retry_call(profile='balanced'), and a streaming iterator that yields ({"delta": "text"}, resume_token). Example code snippet in SDK docs will show integration with 'tenacity' for backoff hooks but we avoid depending on tenacity in core (optional helper package 'redwood-retry').
   - TypeScript: export enum RetryProfile and a top-level client option retry: {profile: 'balanced' | CustomRetryOptions}. Provide a small promise-retry wrapper with built-in jitter and per-attempt hook to emit telemetry events. For streaming, return an AsyncIterable with attached resumeToken property.
   - Go: expose functional options WithRetryProfile(ProfileBalanced) and a helper BackoffStrategy interface. Streaming returns a channel plus a ResumeToken string in the StreamMeta struct.

6) Observability & telemetry:
   - SDK emits metric tags for each retry attempt: retry_count, retry_profile, retry_reason (transient|rate_limited|capacity).
   - Errors surfaced to customers will include a suggested 'retryable' boolean for programmatic handling.

7) Testing / validation plan:
   - Unit tests for mapping HTTP codes -> retry behavior.
   - Integration tests with a local proxy that simulates network flakes, injected Retry-After headers, and server-side idempotency responses (matching/mismatching payloads).
   - Streaming chaos test: kill connection at various sequence offsets and validate resume path and client-visible semantics.

8) Rollout plan:
   - Implement helpers and defaults behind a feature flag (sdk_retry_v2) in all three languages.
   - Start with Beta in Python and TypeScript (broadest usage) and a Go preview.
   - Docs + migration guide, plus code samples and a small interop test harness.

PRs / artifacts:
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/sdk-resilience-presets (placeholder)
- Prototype PR (Python): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/1234
- Crosslang examples repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/pull/78
- Test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reliability-test-harness/pull/45

Open questions / trade-offs recorded:
- Should SDK auto-surface server idempotency TTL? We expose whatever server returns but avoid making server guarantees.
- Streaming resume semantics complicate server state; do we allow resume across different client SDK versions? For now we constrain resume_token format and add a version field.
- Whether to include a default server-side idempotency header if the caller provides an empty string: we will not synthesize. Caller explicitly provides external dedupe keys.

Next steps:
- Implement core RetryProfile and error taxonomy mapping in Python and TS.
- Add unit + integration tests and a PR template for future changes to retry defaults.
- Create docs and sample snippets in quickstart repos.

Acceptance criteria:
- SDKs expose named retry profiles and allow custom overrides.
- Idempotency key behavior documented and implemented for create/mutate endpoints.
- Streaming resume flow implemented in at least Python and TypeScript with a simple example.
- Telemetry tags emitted for retries and retry reasons.
